C++.justification: `template<typename T> T head(const std::vector<T>& xs){ return xs[0]; }` — template result type is exactly T, not erased/boxed; used at int and std::string.

Go.justification: Go 1.18+ generics: func head[T any](s []T) T { return s[0] }; used at []int32 and []string, both with statically recoverable result type T.

Java.justification: static <T> T head(List<T> xs) { return xs.get(0); } — declared result type T is statically recoverable from the generic signature even though erased at runtime; used at Integer and String call sites.

Kotlin.fragment:
fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T = xs[0]
val a = head(listOf(4, 5, 6))
val b = head(listOf("p", "q"))
return a.toString() + b
Kotlin.justification: fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T = xs[0] — parametric function reused at Int and String element types with T recoverable statically at each call site.

Python.fragment:
def head(xs: list[T]) -> T:
    return xs[0]
a = head([4, 5, 6])
b = head(["p", "q"])
return str(a) + b
Python.justification: Per the canonical_task's own named substitution clause: Python has only a universal dynamic type, no enforced parametric generics; the nearest standard (untyped) function form is substituted.

Quidra.citation: language.md 'Generics': `T first<T>(T[] values) return values[0]` is the exact verbatim example of an unconstrained generic function reused at two element types.
Quidra.fragment:
T head<T>(T[] values)
    return values[0]

int a = head([4, 5, 6])
string b = head(["p", "q"])
return a.string() + b
Quidra.justification: language.md 'Generics': `T first<T>(T[] values) return values[0]` is the exact verbatim example of an unconstrained generic function reused at two element types.

Swift.justification: func head<T>(_ xs: [T]) -> T { xs[0] } reused at Int32 and String — Swift generics preserve the T -> T static relationship (no type erasure to Any).

TypeScript.justification: function head<T>(xs:T[]):T{return xs[0];} used at number[] and string[] with T recoverable at each call site.

Zig.justification: fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; } — declaration-level parametric type T with a statically recoverable T->T result relationship, reused at i32 and []const u8.
